title: More Than 5,000 March in Nuevo Laredo's Revolution Day Parade
excerpt: More than 5,000 people took part in Nuevo Laredo's parade marking the 116th anniversary of the Mexican Revolution, with 63 contingents marching down Avenida Guerrero.
content:
More than 5,000 people took part Friday, Nov. 20, in Nuevo Laredo's parade marking the 116th anniversary of the Mexican Revolution.

For two hours, the community gathered along Avenida Guerrero watched 63 contingents pass by, with music and applause, in colorful costumes representing the revolutionary era. Students from public and private schools showed off their talent and creativity, presenting scenes from the era and portrayals of the heroes and heroines who took part in the 1910 struggle. Elaborate floats also drew the crowd's attention.

Civic and military authorities, led by Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal and garrison commander Gen. Humberto Ortega Ramírez, watched the contingents from the stage set up at the Monumento a Los Fundadores, in front of the Municipal Palace. The mayor said she was thrilled to see the parades come alive year after year, with more women and men, young people and children taking part with such joy.

The weather was cloudy and cool, well suited to the outdoor celebration, and the parade ended without any incidents, according to reports from the event.

Sources: El Horizonte, Nov. 20, 2026; Muro Político, Nov. 20, 2026.
